images.filename: Main Street, Castleisland, Co. Kerry - geograph.org.uk - 581627.jpg
images.caption:
Main Street, Castleisland, Co. Kerry, near to Castleisland, Cloonagh Bridge and  Kilcow, Kerry, Ireland.
The town is renowned for the width of its main street � the second widest in Ireland and second only to the famous O'Connell Street in the capital. 

It is always busy with traffic, though, being a junction town for roads (N21, N23, R577) leading in and out of Kerry.

images.filename: Castleisland Courthouse and Carnegie Library - geograph.org.uk - 489134.jpg
images.caption:
Castleisland Courthouse and Carnegie Library The Carnegie Trust Library Building which was designed by R.M. Butler in 1920 was located at the eastern end of Castleisland's main street and burned to the ground in the same year. 
It was subsequently rebuilt on the same site and still functions as the town library. That is until the new library at the western end of the town takes over later this year (2007)

images.caption:
College Road, Castleisland Colourful garden walls frame this road on the outskirts of Castleisland.
Halfway down on the right is St Pat's Boy's College which gives the road its name. 

The road seems to lead to the town's RC church of Saints Stephen and John, however there is no direct route to it.

images.filename: Kerry slugs - forest and bog phenotypes.jpg
images.caption: The Kerry slug Geomalacus maculosus occurs in two colour morphs in Ireland. Brown morphs are associated with forest habitats and black morphs are associated with open habitats such as blanket bog or heath.
